deviations: TDD red proofs first demonstrated the mixed animated/unanimated scope was accepted by domain projection and the editor advertised five ineligible targets.
The first full-suite pass exposed shared-animation coupling in the synthetic domain fixture; the second animated target was corrected to an independent rule/application.

A late external-revision browser refresh intermittently exceeded Playwright’s implicit five-second poll; the proof now uses an explicit 15-second settled-state timeout within its existing 60-second budget.
goalbuddy_receipt_v1.summary: Claim: Hold now fails closed unless every selected target contributes animated tracks with an explicit enter boundary. The editor advertises only eligible targets, and installed Chrome selects two independent animations then proves semantic IDs exactly equal generated Hold track element IDs after durable reload. Top failures—silent mixed-scope acceptance, partial missing-boundary mutation, and misleading UI eligibility—are covered by domain and CLI unchanged-revision rejection plus browser assertions. Two final installed-Chrome receipts were byte-identical (SHA-256 6fd8348a8c5c1f3afba6e8d3cb39c6ce252c75949c64c4e4ba0f000d40a5ec82), with clean diagnostics and privacy guards.
